places.name: Cradle Mountain-Lake St Clair National Park
places.ai_summary: Cradle Mountain-Lake St Clair National Park is a stunning wilderness area in Tasmania, featuring rugged mountains, glacial lakes, and diverse wildlife. It's part of the Tasmanian Wilderness World Heritage Area.
places.name_english: Cradle Mountain-Lake St Clair National Park
places.place_tip: Hike the Dove Lake Circuit for breathtaking views of Cradle Mountain.

places.name: Museum of Old and New Art (MONA)
places.ai_summary: MONA is a world-renowned art museum in Hobart, showcasing provocative and contemporary art pieces. It's a must-visit for art enthusiasts and those seeking a unique cultural experience.
places.name_english: Museum of Old and New Art (MONA)
places.place_tip: Take the MONA ferry for a scenic journey to the museum.

places.name: Freycinet National Park
places.ai_summary: Freycinet National Park is famous for its stunning coastal scenery, including the iconic Wineglass Bay. The park offers a range of outdoor activities and is home to diverse wildlife.
places.place_tip: Visit the Wineglass Bay Lookout for a stunning view of the bay.

places.name: Wineglass Bay
places.ai_summary: Wineglass Bay is a pristine beach located in Freycinet National Park, known for its white sandy beach and crystal-clear waters. It's a popular spot for swimming, kayaking, and picnicking.
places.place_tip: Bring your camera for stunning beach and bay photos.

places.name: Port Arthur Historic Site
places.ai_summary: Port Arthur Historic Site is a former convict settlement and now a UNESCO World Heritage site. It offers a glimpse into Australia's convict past with well-preserved ruins and informative displays.
places.place_tip: Join a guided tour to learn about the history of the site.
places.address: 6973 Arthur Hwy, Port Arthur TAS 7182, Australia

places.name: Salamanca Market (Hobart)
places.ai_summary: Salamanca Market is a vibrant and bustling market in Hobart, offering a wide range of local produce, crafts, and gourmet food. It's a great place to experience the local culture and cuisine.

opening_hours.notes: Open only on weekends and public holidays.

places.place_tip: Try the local cheeses and fresh produce.

places.name: Mount Wellington (kunanyi)
places.ai_summary: Mount Wellington, also known as kunanyi, is a prominent peak near Hobart, offering panoramic views of the city and surrounding landscapes. It's a popular spot for hiking and sightseeing.
places.place_tip: Drive or hike to the summit for breathtaking views.

places.name: Bay of Fires
places.ai_summary: The Bay of Fires is a coastal area in Tasmania, known for its white sandy beaches, clear blue waters, and striking orange lichen-covered rocks. It's a great spot for swimming, snorkeling, and relaxing.
places.place_tip: Explore the walking trails for stunning coastal views.

places.name: Bruny Island
places.ai_summary: Bruny Island is a picturesque island located off the southeast coast of Tasmania, known for its stunning landscapes, wildlife, and gourmet food. It's a popular destination for a day trip from Hobart.
places.place_tip: Visit the Bruny Island Cheese Co. for local cheese and produce.

places.name: Tasman National Park
places.ai_summary: Tasman National Park is known for its dramatic coastal cliffs, secluded beaches, and rich wildlife. The park offers a range of walking tracks and is a great place for birdwatching.
places.place_tip: Take the Three Capes Track for stunning views of the coastline.

places.name: Cataract Gorge Reserve
places.ai_summary: Cataract Gorge Reserve is a beautiful natural reserve located near Launceston, featuring stunning gorge views, walking trails, and a swimming pool. It's a great spot for a day trip and picnicking.
places.place_tip: Take the chairlift for a unique view of the gorge.
places.address: Cataract Gorge Reserve, Launceston TAS 7250, Australia

places.name: Maria Island National Park
places.ai_summary: Maria Island National Park is a beautiful and remote island park, known for its stunning beaches, wildlife, and historic ruins. It's a great place for hiking, camping, and exploring.
places.place_tip: Explore the Painted Cliffs for a unique geological formation.

places.name: Bonorong Wildlife Sanctuary
places.ai_summary: Bonorong Wildlife Sanctuary is a wildlife rescue and rehabilitation center, where visitors can see and learn about Tasmania's unique wildlife, including kangaroos, koalas, and Tasmanian devils.
places.place_tip: Join a guided tour to learn about the wildlife rescue efforts.

places.name: Royal Tasmanian Botanical Gardens
places.ai_summary: The Royal Tasmanian Botanical Gardens is a beautiful and historic botanical garden, featuring a diverse collection of plants from Tasmania and around the world. It's a great place for a leisurely stroll and enjoying nature.
places.place_tip: Don't miss the Subantarctic Plant House.

attribution.title: City of Hobart Flag
attribution.author:
I.G. Anderson

derivative work: Squiresy92
attribution.description:
The flag of Hobart City Council, of Tasmania, Australia. Designed in 1951 by Hobart architect and alderman, I.G. Anderson and first flown in 1953.
The star is derived from the arms of Lord Hobart, 4th Earl of Buckinghamshire (1760-1816), Secretary of State for War and the Colonies at the time of colonial settlement (1804), and after whom Hobart is named. The colour used on the arms Lord Hobart was, in fact, sable (black), rather than blue.

The red lion is from the Tasmanian flag - and its location at the top of the shield signifies Hobart's position as the Capital City.

places.name: Gordon River Cruise
places.ai_summary: The Gordon River Cruise is a scenic boat cruise in Tasmania, offering stunning views of the Gordon River, rainforests, and wildlife. It's a great way to experience the natural beauty of Tasmania.
places.place_tip: Bring a jacket, it can be cool on the water.

attribution.description: A Metro Scania L94UB 14.5m bus with Volgren CR224L body is pictured in the Hobart bus mall. The original three Volgren 14.5m buses were later joined by an L94UB with a Northcoast body which replaced a bus destroyed by fire.

places.name: Mount Field National Park
places.ai_summary: Mount Field National Park is known for its stunning natural beauty, including waterfalls, tall trees, and diverse wildlife. The park offers a range of walking tracks and is a great place for a day trip from Hobart.
places.place_tip: Visit the Tall Trees Walk for a chance to see the world's tallest trees.
places.address: Mount Field National Park, Tasmania, Australia

places.name: The Nut (Stanley)
places.ai_summary: The Nut is a flat-topped hill located in Stanley, Tasmania, offering stunning views of the surrounding area. It's a popular spot for hiking and photography.
places.place_tip: Take the chairlift or hike to the top for stunning views.

places.name: Franklin-Gordon Wild Rivers National Park
places.ai_summary: Franklin-Gordon Wild Rivers National Park is a remote and rugged wilderness area in Tasmania, known for its stunning river gorges, waterfalls, and diverse wildlife. It's a great place for experienced hikers and nature enthusiasts.
places.place_tip: Visit the Gordon River for a chance to see the rare orange-bellied parrot.
places.address: Franklin-Gordon Wild Rivers National Park, Tasmania, Australia

places.name: Hastings Caves State Reserve
places.ai_summary: Hastings Caves State Reserve is known for its stunning limestone caves and beautiful natural surroundings. The reserve offers guided tours of the caves and has picnic facilities.
places.place_tip: Wear comfortable shoes for the cave tour.
places.address: Hastings Caves Rd, Hastings TAS 7109, Australia

places.name: Richmond Bridge
places.ai_summary: Richmond Bridge is a historic sandstone arch bridge located in Richmond, Tasmania. It's the oldest bridge still in use in Australia and is a popular spot for photography and picnicking.
places.place_tip: Explore the nearby historic village of Richmond.
